newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Gaddafi calls for pan-Arab unified state.
newsitem.headline: Gaddafi calls for pan-Arab unified state.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi called on Libyans to march in favour of a unified state that would comprise the territories of Egypt, Tunisia, Sudan and Libya, the official Libyan news agency JANA reported on Sunday.
Tripoli-based Western diplomats said the call marked a return of Gaddafi to his active militantcy for Arab unity after a more pragmatic stand over the past few years.

"You must impose unity with Egypt, with Tunisia, with Sudan, and with Arab neighbouring countries, not by forces, but by pressures of the masses...the marches for unity must not stop," Gaddafi said in a speech on Saturday night.
In the 1970s and 1980s, Gaddafi's supporters marched to Egypt and Tunisia to push for a lifting of borders, but the people were always stopped at the borders.
"At the start of this year starts the pressures for merger, the marches for unity, ignoring the artifical borders set up by the colonialism..., because we are a single Arab nation," he said.
The Libyan leader was talking at a rally in the southern Libyan city of Sebha where 20 years ago he proclamed the "power of the masses". His comments were monitored in Tunis.

A Western diplomat said: "This is a shift, because during the last years, Gaddafi seemed to have moderated his pan-Arab enthusiasm and persuaded his neighbouring countries that he was for a progressive action to build unity without any interference in internal affairs."
